title: Backbone as Duplex Process Channel
description: Replace the vcs crate's Backbone abstraction (currently one-shot load()/sync(json) pull-push with temp:// as a fake "temporary" backbone) with a duplex message-channel model: there is always exactly one WIP graph in memory (initial projection + edit/change/checkpoint/alternative history), and a Backbone, when attached, is always a bidirectional channel to another process (WASM plugin <-> host, host <-> remote) used only to synchronize. Delete temp:// / BackboneKind::Temporary / TemporaryBackbone entirely; "detached" (no backbone) becomes the default and replaces it. Move persistence (file/folder/localStorage) host-side behind the channel via a BackboneStorage trait consumed by a StorageBackbone endpoint. Close the framework/sync sync-gap where OpEnvelopes were ingested but never re-materialized into the vcs edit timeline. Update wit contract (backbone-read/write -> backbone-send/backbone-poll), plugin host, os core, hub, s crates, wgpu renderer, and TS surfaces accordingly. Full design plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/vcs-there-is-always-encapsulated-wombat.md.
summary:
Replaced the vcs crate's document backbone with a duplex message-channel model, matching the directive that there is always exactly one WIP graph in memory and an optional backbone exists only to synchronize it with another process.

Design: `Backbone::{send, receive}` exchanges `BackboneMessage::{Snapshot, Ops}` instead of the old one-shot `load()`/`sync()`. `DocumentVcsStore` gained `attach_backbone`/`attach_backbone_uri`/`detach_backbone`/`tick`/`ingest_remote`; `dispatch` now pumps inbound messages before every command and flushes outbound after (a single `OpEnvelope` for `Apply`, a full snapshot for every structural command). `BackboneKind`/`TemporaryBackbone`/`temp://` are deleted entirely — "detached" (`None`) is the resting state and default. `framework/core`'s kernel absorbed `OpDag`/`InsertResult` (moved from `framework/sync`) with a new `drain_applied_envelopes()`, closing the sync gap: `SyncSession` now wraps a `DocumentVcsStore` and `receive()` actually materializes remote envelopes into the edit timeline (previously it only buffered them in the DAG and never touched vcs history). `FileJsonBackbone`/`FolderSqliteBackbone`/`RemoteBackbone` are now native-only, built on a new `BackboneStorage` primitive (`FileJsonStorage`/`FolderSqliteStorage`); inside any wasm sandbox, `resolve_backbone` always returns `PortBackbone`, which forwards over a new `BackboneChannelPort`/`backbone-send`/`backbone-poll` wit contract to the host process, which resolves the real backbone on its own (native) side — modeling the actual process boundary the directive asked for. The pre-existing keyed `BackbonePort`/`MemoryBackbonePort`/`LocalStorageBackbonePort` KV-store primitive (used for OS studio catalog/presence, unrelated to per-document sync) was left untouched.

Verified: vcs (20/20 tests, including a new `MemoryBackbone::pair` bidirectional duplex test and an attach-reconciles-a-persisted-snapshot test), framework-core (kernel OpDag drain-order test), framework-sync (2/2, including a receive-materializes-into-timeline test proving the gap is closed), framework-plugin + framework-plugin-host (17/17), s_studio/s-plugin/os-core/os-hub/wgpu-renderer all compile clean, and the react renderer's vitest suite (80/80, including updated sync-tools tests). os-hub's new GET /documents/{id}/ops?since= route verified via `cargo check --tests` (full test binary compiles) after the shared build lock stayed contended by a concurrent session's workspace-wide test run; the route logic was traced by hand and is straightforward version filtering.
